newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index down 2.5 percent in November.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index down 2.5 percent in November.

text.p: The Kuwait Stock Exchange share index fell 47.8 points to 1,906.4 points in November, the exchange said on Wednesday.

Traders have said warnings by Kuwaiti officials about "aggressive intentions" by former occupier Iraq and U.S. concern over regional power Iran seeking control on the region's oil reserves were among the reasons for the decline.
Value of traded shares fell 44.7 percent to 725.5 million dinars ($2.426 billion) in November. Volume dropped 57.3 percent to 2.331 billion shares compared to a 22 percent rise in October.
The bourse, which has 58 listed shares and a capitalisation of about 4.1 billion dinars, operates for 2-1/2 hours five days a week (Saturday-Wednesday).
Banks were the most active by value with 31.6 percent of total trade value. Investment firms came second with 18.7 percent folowed by services with 18.3 percent.

Only nationals of the Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the Kuwait exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds run by local firms.
